title: The Word For Today. Standing Appointment.
content:
If the perfect, sinless Son of God required a non-negotiable, intentional time of solitude to connect with the Father, how do we expect our spiritual lives to survive without one?

We live our lives enslaved to the ding of notifications, the weight of overflowing calendars, and the relentless demands of our daily routines. We diligently schedule dentist visits, oil changes, and business meetings, protecting those blocks of time with fierce determination. Yet, when it comes to the most vital relationship in our lives, we often offer God only the leftover crumbs of our day. We promise to pray "when things slow down," but they never do.

In Mark 1:35, we witness a masterclass in priorities. The night before, Jesus had been inundated by a chaotic crowd of sick and demon-possessed people at Peter's doorstep. He was undoubtedly exhausted. Yet, His immediate response to a demanding schedule was not to sleep in, but to slip away. He modeled what it means to keep a standing appointment with the Father.

Here are three guiding lessons for our consideration.

1. The Priority of the Appointment.
Jesus did not fit prayer into a gap in His schedule; He built His schedule around prayer. By rising "very early in the morning, while it was still dark," He gave the Father His first and absolute best.
The Principle: True devotion requires us to seek God before the world has a chance to make demands on our time.
The Practice: We must transition from an "if I have time" mindset to a "first things first" commitment.

2. The Place of the Appointment.
Intimacy requires isolation. Jesus intentionally "left the house and went off to a solitary place." He knew that the noise of the house and the expectations of the crowd would easily choke out quiet communion.
The Principle: To hear the still, small voice of God, we must intentionally unplug from the loud, persistent voices of retail, news, and social media.
The Practice: Find a physical space — a specific chair, a quiet room, or a porch — that serves as your designated sanctuary for stillness.

3. The Purpose of the Appointment.
Jesus did not go to the lonely place to hide, to escape His calling, or to lazily unwind. The text explicitly states that He went there to pray. His purpose was absolute alignment and deep communion with the Father.
The Principle: Our personal devotional time is not an exercise in ticking off a spiritual checklist; it is the vital fuel line for our souls.
The Practice: Protect this time solely for the purpose of talking to God, reading His Word, and listening for His clear direction.

Ellen White Insight:
"Consecrate yourself to God in the morning; make this your very first work. Let your prayer be, 'Take me, O Lord, as wholly Thine. I lay all my plans at Thy feet. Use me today in Thy service. Abide with me, and let all my work be wrought in Thee.' This is a daily matter. Each morning consecrate yourself to God for that day. Surrender all your plans to Him, to be carried out or given up as His providence shall indicate. Thus day by day you may be giving your life into the hands of God, and thus your life will be molded more and more after the life of Christ." — Steps to Christ, p. 70

The Appeal:
Do not let the demands of a busy day crowd out the One who gives you breath to live it. When you skip your time with God, you try to carry burdens you were never meant to bear alone. Prioritize the Creator over the creation today. Decide right now that your meeting with Him is non-negotiable, because a life aligned with God is too important to leave to chance.

Today's Declaration:
"My time with God is my most important meeting today. I will not give Him my leftovers, and I will protect our appointment above all other demands."

Further Reading:
Psalm 5:3 — Giving God your first and best moments in the morning.
Luke 10:38-42 — Choosing the "one thing necessary" over endless busyness.
Matthew 6:33 — Seeking His kingdom first, knowing He provides the rest.
reflection: What specific distraction usually tempts you to reschedule your time with God, and what boundary can you set to protect that appointment tomorrow morning?
prayer: Heavenly Father, forgive me for letting the noise of the world push You to the sidelines. Give me the strength to say 'no' to distractions so I can say 'yes' to You. Help me anchor my day in Your presence, trusting that everything else will fall into place. Amen.
keyVerse: Very early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up, left the house and went off to a solitary place, where he prayed.
